executiveSummary: Meppel was fresh and pending when claimed: its artifact was absent and the generated manifest named task municipality_gm0119. Its official/generated 2025 identity, 36,271 residents, 46 neighbourhoods, fourteen districts, five BAG woonplaatsen, nine BRT settlement labels, seven logical road-border records, Meppel station and 49 scheduled-transit stop areas are coherent. Neighbourhood rows total 36,275 residents, four above the municipal control (+0.011%), which the allocator reconciles without rewriting published observations. All ten presets run deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services with finite bounds, exact no-event behavior, causal-ledger closure, service-layer invariance and monotone event burden. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Meppel has a real and unusually coupled high-water mechanism: upstream Drenthe water converges through canals and streams into the Meppelerdiep, whose discharge depends on the Rijkswaterstaat Meppelerdiepsluis and the external WDODelta Zedemuden pumping system toward the Zwarte Water. A documented October 2023 sluice failure rapidly raised levels around Meppel; Ootmaanlanden storage outside the municipality was created to limit Meppel flooding. The canonical preset is instead named Rhine, Meuse & IJssel high water and selects none of these boundaries, structures or storages, yet holds exactly 1.051851 m and severity 0.331498 from T+12 through T+72, reports 15,409 affected people-equivalent and 994,139.376 deprived person-hours at T+72. Eight materially different nonzero single-hazard T+24 runs reuse the same complete neighbourhood rank, contradicting water-system, cloudburst, heat, smoke and cyber mechanisms. Public registers add 93 partial water assets—61 weirs, 22 surface-water pumps, five sluices, four sewer pumps and rwzi Meppel—plus one Meppel Hoofdvaart Waterinfo observation, one Enexis planning sample, 67 antennas, forty education locations and Isala Meppel acute-care context, but not complete live topology, state, backup or restoration. Meppel is also a national rail bottleneck: ProRail says the only route between the northern network and the rest of the Netherlands runs via Meppel, yet the model has no rail flows or incident state. A28/A32/N371/N375, waterborne industrial/logistics areas, Isala, five dispersed woonplaatsen and response destinations require time-valid multimodal access. The municipal sewer plan explicitly describes pump-power failure causing sewage release and only partial telemetry. Public heat cooling locations were announced for opening hours during an August 2026 episode, not as all-hazard shelters; no reviewed public source confirms 72-hour emergency support points, resources, hospital acceptance, household stock or operator restoration. Unknown water, sluice, pump, road, rail, hospital, utility, support, visitor and industrial state remains Unknown or NoData, never safe or zero.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0119 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, woonplaats and settlement inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated CBS/BAG/BRT snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; audited 3 September 2026
supports: The annual official/generated row identifies GM0119 as Meppel and reports 36,271 residents, density 654/km², 21.2% aged 65-plus and 6,686 one-person households. CBS/PDOK is CC BY 4.0 and demographic context, not incident occupancy or individual vulnerability.

The municipality reference point [6.189380364979077,52.70399058588146] lies inside the generalized 2025 boundary. The outline is suitable for selection and aggregation, not hydraulic, sewer, rail, road or facility connectivity.

Forty-six neighbourhood rows in fourteen districts sum to 36,275 residents (+4, +0.011%), 16,915 households and 7,695 independently rounded residents aged 65-plus. The allocator reconciles to the municipality control without altering source observations.

BAG supplies Broekhuizen, De Schiphorst, Meppel, Nijeveen and Rogat; BRT supplies nine locality labels. BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and BRT is CC BY 4.0; place, label and demographic provenance remains distinct.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Meppelerdiep cross-boundary discharge, Zedemuden and documented sluice failure
evidenceSources.edition: Current operator pages inspected 3 September 2026; Meppelerdiepsluis incident update 21 October 2023; Ootmaanlanden update 8 June 2026
supports: WDODelta says Zedemuden at Zwartsluis pumps Meppelerdiep water into the Zwarte Water during wet periods to prevent water nuisance/flooding across a roughly 92,000-hectare system. Its three pumps have a stated design total of 124 m³/s and cross-authority operation is governed by the Meppelerdiep–Overijsselse Vecht water agreement.

On 21 October 2023 a technical failure at the Rijkswaterstaat Meppelerdiepsluis prevented discharge, rapidly raised water around Zwartsluis and Meppel and flooded some gardens. Manual opening of sluice-door gates restored discharge. This is historical event evidence, not current failure or a forecast.

The 2023 report shows wind, external water levels, shipping depth, woonboats, dike stability, sluice position and Zedemuden operating constraints interact. A pump's nameplate capacity alone does not establish usable incident capacity or direction.

Ootmaanlanden storage near Uffelte was built in 2024 to hold water during extreme rain and help prevent Meppel flooding; a June 2026 control failure unintentionally filled it. External storage/control is a real dependency but neither event establishes its current state. No standard reuse licence or machine operational cadence is stated.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Meppel / Waterschap Drents Overijsselse Delta / Het Waterschapshuis
evidenceSources.title: E03 — Municipal rain, groundwater, sewer and partial managed-water context
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal Riolering en Water Programma 2023–2028; current local water pages inspected and HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: The municipal programme says sewer pumps are essential, wastewater can be released into buildings, streets or surface water after defect/power failure, and municipal pumps have only partial telemetry for remote 24-hour management. It separates municipal and water-board pumping responsibilities.

Meppel describes itself as water-rich with construction groundwater/flow risks along the Reest, diverted Hoogeveense Vaart and around Oosterboer/Isala Reestdal/Wold Aa. Its climate page uses a peak-rain example up to 70 mm in one hour and separately identifies heat and drought.

WDODelta says Oosterboer is low-lying and depends on pumping during heavy rain and seepage. The Oude Vaart plan seeks slower flow and storage for both heavy rain and drought. These are local mechanism/project facts, not live footprint or probability.

The partial HWH assignment contains 93 points: 61 weirs, 22 surface-water pumps, five sluices, four sewer pumps and rwzi Meppel. The CC BY-SA 4.0 contributor-dependent inventory does not establish complete topology, compatible capacity units, telemetry, live state, power, backup or restoration; null stays Unknown.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Timestamped Hoofdvaart observation and official flood-scenario semantics
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO 2025.1.6; Waterinfo observation retrieved 2 September 2026; audited 3 September 2026
supports: LIWO provides professional flood layers and recommends water-manager expertise. Primary, regional and water-system flood cases have distinct source, trajectory/breach, boundary, probability, depth, velocity, arrival and recession semantics; a maximum map is not current truth.

The deployed Waterinfo snapshot assigns Meppel Hoofdvaart one fresh water-level observation: -17 cm NAP at 2026-09-02T17:30Z. There is no municipality-assigned Waterinfo forecast feature through T+72.
Waterinfo is CC0, public and non-mission-critical. One point/datum/time does not establish Meppelerdiep, Reest, Wold Aa, storage, sluice, pump or sewer state, nor a municipal inundation surface.
Missing forecasts, unselected scenarios and uncovered cells remain NoData/Unknown, not normal level, operational structure, zero flood or all-clear.

evidenceSources.publisher: ProRail / Rijkswaterstaat / Provincie Drenthe / OVapi / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E05 — National rail bottleneck, road network and Isala acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: ProRail page updated 22 May 2026; NWB-Light 1 August 2026; OVapi retrieved 3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: ProRail says the only rail route between the northern Netherlands and the rest of the country passes Meppel and a disruption affects traffic to/from the entire north. Zwolle–Meppel is a bottleneck; works through 2034 target capacity, power-supply robustness and a fourth platform.

Seven monthly CC0 NWB border records cover A28, A32, N371 and N375 to De Wolden, Staphorst, Westerveld and Steenwijkerland. Repeated A28/A32/N375 sides are series/shared physical corridors, not additive capacity; 260/150 values are logical scenario units.

Meppel station and 49 in-boundary GTFS stop areas are static location/schedule context, not live train/bus state, rolling stock, capacity, accessibility or evacuation transport. The provincial N375 is also an official A28/A32 calamity diversion, so simultaneous availability must not be assumed.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 CC0 assigns Isala Meppel: 24/7 emergency department, no acute obstetrics, ten reported treatment rooms and 10,247 emergency visits in 2025. Questionnaire/history does not establish current occupancy, acceptance, staffing, access, power/water, medicines, backup or restoration.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Meppel / Provincie Drenthe / Port of Zwolle
evidenceSources.title: E06 — Waterborne industry, port, hazardous-material and visitor/logistics pathways
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal business/haven pages inspected 3 September 2026; external-safety policy is older static planning context
supports: The municipality identifies Oevers A–D and Oude Vaart as water-related industrial/logistics areas along the Drentsche Hoofdvaart, Meppelerdiep and Sethehaven; Oevers D serves ships up to 2,000 tonnes and A28/A32/N375 connections.

The province manages the Drenthe part of Meppelerdiep; municipal locks/bridges have published recurring hours and the harbour serves professional/recreational users. A schedule is not an incident-time navigability, bridge, lock, vessel or port-capacity observation.

Older official external-safety planning identifies container/fertiliser/feed movements, higher industrial categories, gas transmission and 110 kV corridors as relevant mechanisms. This is static eligibility/context, not current inventory, route, leak/fire probability or exclusion zone.
Industrial workers, vessels, visitors and through freight are not captured by resident population. Public pages state no standard machine incident cadence or reuse licence.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Meppel / Enexis / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Electricity congestion and partial communication/education context
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal page current under rules effective 1 July 2026; snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026
supports: Meppel says net congestion limits or delays new/expanded connections and that timing varies by area. Its August 2026 project-prioritisation notice explicitly says municipal submission does not guarantee allocation. Planning constraint is not a current outage or household continuity forecast.

One NBNL postcode sample maps to Enexis area MP Meppel and reports existing/required withdrawal 79.8/78.2 MW, a 26.7 MW/84-request withdrawal queue, injection planning/queue, thirteen projects and earliest year 2026. One sample is not full municipal topology, live load, reserve, switching or restoration; exact licence identifier was not found.

RDI assigns 67 installations—four broadcast, twelve fixed-link, 31 mobile, one other-mobile and nineteen amateur—and DUO assigns forty education locations across primary, secondary, vocational/adult, special and higher education. RDI has no stated standard licence/fixed cadence; DUO is attribution-licensed and daily.
Public points do not prove telecom coverage/backhaul/power, live school occupancy, shelter/support role, staffing, stock, backup or operation.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Meppel / Veiligheidsregio Drenthe / KNMI / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Preparedness, heat action and other-hazard monitoring limits
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal heat notice published 13 August 2026; current public safety/context pages and monitoring snapshot inspected 3 September 2026
supports: During an August 2026 warm episode the municipality named three cooling spaces during their opening hours and called for attention to older, chronically ill and single residents. That time-specific measure is not an all-hazard shelter, overnight facility or currently active response commitment.

Municipal/regional crisis responsibilities support warning, public care, primary needs, environmental care, information and aftercare. No reviewed current public source confirms Meppel emergency support points, 72-hour capacity, stock, staff, generator, water, offline communication or accessibility.

No KNMI weather station, RIVM PM2.5 point or recent seismic origin lies inside GM0119 in the deployed snapshot. Absence of a local point/event is NoData in that bounded feed, not proof of zero weather, heat, smoke, ground or air-quality risk.

Canonical coastal is a wind-only exercise locally, wildfire is remote Veluwe smoke, earthquake is a Groningen-source exercise and cyber has no named target. They remain synthetic planning screens unless event, forecast, target or plume evidence is selected.

residualLimitations: This deterministic 72-hour planning stress test is not a WDODelta, Rijkswaterstaat, KNMI, VRD, Meppel, ProRail, Isala or operator forecast, warning, probability, evacuation order, casualty estimate or restoration promise.
No selected Meppelerdiep/Zwarte Water hydrograph, wind/external level, sluice/pump/storage state, official footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, probability or NoData mask is ingested.
The 1.051851 m property is a synthetic screening value, not observed or officially modeled local metres and must not drive evacuation, route, care, port or service thresholds.
The generalized boundary and centre do not resolve waterways, storage, controls, land levels, drains, buildings, roads, rail, industrial areas, assets, households or individuals.
CBS values are rounded/suppressed; the +4 population difference and null district-heat/charging/other fields are publication semantics, not extra/zero people or assets.
HWH is partial and 93 points do not establish complete topology, compatible units, telemetry, power, backup or restoration; null remains Unknown.
The 2023 sluice failure and 2026 Ootmaanlanden event are historical observations, not current state, recurrence probability or forecast.
Zedemuden design capacity does not prove available incident capacity, direction, access, staff, power, control or recovery.
One Hoofdvaart Waterinfo point is datum/time-specific and non-mission-critical; no municipal forecast through T+72 is NoData, not normal water or safety.
No complete public causal Enexis feeder/switching, Vitens pipe/pressure/quality, gas district, municipal sewer or telecom backhaul/restoration topology is authorized in the model.
One NBNL sample is planning/queue context rather than municipal coverage, current load, outage, reserve, switching or restoration.
RDI sites do not establish coverage, traffic, backhaul, power/backup, damage, availability or restoration; standard licence/fixed cadence is unstated.
NWB, ProRail and GTFS are static context and do not establish incident road/rail/bus/waterway throughput, rolling stock, evacuation, response, care or logistics continuity.
RIVM Isala questionnaire data does not establish present occupancy, acceptance, staffing, ambulance access, diversion, power/water, medicines, generator fuel or backup endurance.
DUO locations do not establish command, reception, shelter, care or distribution roles; no all-hazard support-point network/capacity was confirmed.
August cooling rooms were valid only within the published heat context/opening hours and are not automatically active, overnight, shelters or all-hazard support sites.
No local KNMI weather, RIVM PM2.5 or recent seismic point is available; absence is not zero exposure, ground motion, weather or safety.
Canonical wildfire lacks local ignition/perimeter/fuel/plume; earthquake is remote Groningen; cyber lacks named target/architecture/detection; compound mixes unvalidated assumptions.
Port/industrial cargo, hazardous materials, workers, vessels, visitors and through rail/road users are not represented by resident population or generic business/supply weights.
Household 72-hour preparedness, stock and ability to assist are not measured; 72 hours is an operations horizon, not guaranteed aid or recovery.

Event-attributable service person-hours is a matched-no-event weighted availability proxy, not measured customer outage-hours, simultaneous deprivation, casualties, displacement or welfare loss; six-hour checkpoints miss rapid control failures and 72 hours excludes prolonged flood/cleanup/reconstruction.
